1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18:

20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page

  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page

  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page

Keyboard:

Mouse:

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs

  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab

Storage:

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete browser-playable 3D open-world superhero game with city traversal, missions, villains, NPC interaction, drowning, menus, credits, and voice lines.

## Requirements
- Create an original 3D city, not copied from any existing Spider-Man game.
- Add super villains, voiced dialogue, villains including Venom, Sandman, Green Goblin, and additional villains.
- Add MJ.
- Add swinging and wall climbing.
- Make the city open world with cars and NPCs.
- Add NPC interaction.
- Include water where the hero can drown.
- Add missions, pause/main menus, credits, and a roughly two-hour campaign structure.
- Support desktop and mobile touch controls.

## Decisions
- Used a browser-based Three.js implementation with procedural geometry.
- Replaced the exact requested Spider-Man/Spider-Man 2 references with an original hero and original city while preserving the requested broad game archetype.
- Implemented the game as a single-screen 3D scene with HTML overlays and browser speech synthesis.
- Added a two-hour-scale mission progression as eight missions rather than timed full-duration content.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with main menu, pause menu, credits, HUD, mission UI, and touch controls.
- Created `style.css` with responsive desktop/mobile presentation.
- Created `game.js` with a Three.js 3D city, roads, buildings, waterfront, cars, NPCs, hero model, missions, boss targets, collision setup, camera, movement, water, drowning, dialogue, and menu logic.
- Added procedural 36-person civilian population and 18 moving cars.
- Added eight mission threads and eight mission locations.
- Added enemy target types for signals, rescues, and bosses.
- Added browser speech synthesis voice lines.
- Added desktop keyboard controls and mobile touch controls.
- Fixed an identified apostrophe syntax issue in a mission voice line.
- Syntax-checked `game.js` successfully.

### Active
- Current work is not yet extended with MJ, Venom, Sandman, Green Goblin, NPC dialogue/interactions, wall climbing, or the requested enhanced villain roster.

### Blocked
- No implementation blocker exists; the remaining enhancement work is unimplemented feature scope.

## Next Move
1. Open `game.js` and add named villain definitions for Venom, Sandman, Green Goblin, and others.
2. Add villain-specific models, attacks, voice lines, and boss mission entries.
3. Add an MJ NPC model and proximity interaction dialogue.
4. Add NPC interaction prompts and unique responses.
5. Add wall-climbing movement by detecting building collision surfaces and switching hero motion state.
6. Enhance swinging with attachment anchors and momentum-based camera/flight behavior.
7. Run a browser server, open the game, and capture and inspect a desktop screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Game markup, overlays, HUD, menus, mission UI, and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: Full visual system and mobile layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Three.js world, movement, missions, combat, NPCs, water, and game logic.

## Important Context
- `game.js` imports Three.js directly from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- The game server can be run with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `game.js` passed `node --input-type=module --check < game.js`.
- MJ and the named villains Venom, Sandman, and Green Goblin remain to be added.
- Wall climbing and fully momentum-based swinging remain to be added.
- NPC interactions currently do not include a dialogue system; mission rescues only hide the NPC model and advance mission progress.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete browser-playable 3D open-world superhero adventure with traversal, missions, villains, NPC interaction, drowning, menus, credits, and voice lines.

## Requirements
- Create an original 3D city and hero; do not copy existing Spider-Man games.
- Include Venom, Sandman, Green Goblin, other villains, MJ, villain voice lines, swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPCs and interactions, and water where the hero can drown.
- Include missions, pause/main menus, credits, a roughly two-hour campaign structure, and desktop/mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based Three.js implementation with procedural geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Preserve the broad superhero-game archetype with original character names and designs.
- Represent the campaign as eight mission threads rather than two hours of timed content.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing project includes menus, HUD, credits, mission progression, procedural city, civilians, cars, waterfront, drowning, combat targets, speech synthesis, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Added procedural villain roster/models and MJ/NPC dialogue code to `game.js`.
- Ran `node --input-type=module --check < game.js` successfully after those additions and attempted patches.

### Active
- Integrate the villain roster into boss missions and add mission-specific villain dialogue; the attempted exact-text replacements reported missing mission-entry and boss-preparation matches.
- Finish MJ/NPC proximity interactions, wall climbing, and improved swinging; attempted replacements for interaction and movement logic also reported missing matches.
- Review actual current `game.js` state, since tool output did not confirm whether earlier edits persisted consistently.

### Blocked
- Exact-string edits failed with `MISSING` reports for mission entries, villain spawning, interaction handling, and climb/swing hooks; no confirmed integration of those pieces.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `game.js` around villain definitions, mission declarations, `prepareMission()`, `interact()`, and `update()`.
2. Apply focused patches using the exact current text or a structured edit, ensuring villain missions use `makeVillain()` and villain dialogue.
3. Wire MJ and NPC proximity dialogue into `interact()`.
4. Implement and verify wall climbing and momentum-based swinging.
5. Run syntax checks and launch the game in a browser to verify gameplay and rendering.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Scene, characters, missions, interactions, movement, and gameplay logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Game overlays, menus, HUD, and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: Responsive visual layout and presentation.

## Important Context
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- A local server can be run with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The last reported syntax check passed, but the latest script printed multiple `MISSING` notices; changes to key mission and movement hooks are not verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a browser-playable original 3D superhero city adventure with traversal, missions, villains, NPCs, shops, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Add a head-on final fight against Venom, with a bonded symbiote shard that unlocks switching between the Afterlight and black suits.

## Requirements
- Keep the hero, city, characters, and dialogue original; avoid copying existing Spider-Man games.
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, and voice lines.
- Provide shops, street details, and clear controls.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a final “VENOM: THE LAST BOND” mission with an enlarged Venom model, eight-hit boss health, and a shard/bond unlock on defeat.
- Added visual Afterlight and black suit materials plus `Q`, HUD-button, and mobile-button suit switching.
- Added four named street-level storefronts; interacting nearby restores up to 35 health, with a cooldown.
- Updated the on-screen controls to include suit switching.
- `node --input-type=module --check < game.js` passed.

### Active
- Verify the updated game in-browser, including the final fight, shard unlock, suit shifting, shops, and mobile controls.
- Inspect/fix any runtime, UI, or gameplay issues found during verification.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not yet been performed. A prior attempt to start a server on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`; the suggested existing URL `http://localhost:3002` has not been confirmed to serve the current project.

## Next Move
1. Check whether `http://localhost:3002` serves the current project; otherwise start the app on an available port.
2. Test mission progression through the final boss, Venom’s defeat and shard unlock, both suit appearances, shop healing, and desktop/mobile controls.
3. Fix any issues and rerun the `game.js` syntax check.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: World, shops, missions, boss combat, suit switching, and gameplay logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: HUD, controls, suit panel, menus, and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: HUD and suit-panel styling, responsive presentation.

## Important Context
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Current boss strikes are triggered by clicking near a boss or interacting with its objective.
- The final mission is appended after the existing campaign threads; the “CONTINUE PATROL” button advances mission index modulo the mission list length.
- Changes have not been browser-verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city story adventure with traversal, missions, characters, shops, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Make the story campaign take about two hours to finish.

## Requirements
- Keep the hero, city, characters, and dialogue original; avoid copying existing games.
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- MJ is a woman; give her, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom.
- “Fix every bug You find”
- Campaign should take two hours to finish.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a final “VENOM: THE LAST BOND” mission with an eight-hit boss health pool and shard/bond unlock on defeat.
- Added Afterlight and black suit materials plus `Q`, HUD-button, and mobile-button suit switching.
- Added four named storefronts; interacting nearby restores up to 35 health with a cooldown.
- Added suit switching to the on-screen controls.
- Added intro-screen markup and basic procedural long/short hair silhouettes in `game.js`.

### Active
- Finish the character face details and explicitly specify MJ as a woman with long hair; add appropriate villain hair where applicable.
- Add intro-screen styling in `style.css` and connect `#intro-start` to the game-start flow.
- Expand the campaign and pacing to support the requested two-hour completion time.
- Verify gameplay, fix discovered bugs, and rerun syntax checks.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior attempt to start a server on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.
- A `functions.edit` attempt to add face details failed because the exact source text did not match; the relevant implementation remains around lines 101–116 of `game.js`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and update `makePerson` in `game.js` to add face features, ensure MJ is explicitly configured as a woman with long hair, and add suitable villain hair while excluding Venom.
2. Style `#intro-screen` and add a start handler for `#intro-start`.
3. Plan campaign content and mission pacing for an approximately two-hour story.
4. Run `node --input-type=module --check < game.js`, launch or locate a server on an available port, and verify core game flows; fix issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Character models, missions, boss combat, suit switching, and game-start handlers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Intro screen, HUD, menus, credits, and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: UI and responsive styling; intro styles are still needed.

## Important Context
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Current intro markup uses `#intro-screen` and `#intro-start`, but no JavaScript handler or CSS has been added.
- `makePerson` accepts `gender` and `longHair` options, but existing NPC creation does not explicitly set gender; face details are unfinished.
- Final mission is appended after existing campaign threads; “CONTINUE PATROL” advances mission index modulo the mission list length.
- `node --input-type=module --check < game.js` passed before the latest character edits; latest edits have not been syntax-checked.
- Working files are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `style.css`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Add numerous cinematic story scenes and make the hero bond with a piece of Venom during their first fight, keeping it for the rest of the game.

## Requirements
- Keep the hero, city, characters, and dialogue original; avoid copying existing games.
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- MJ is a woman; give her, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom.
- “Fix every bug You find”
- Campaign should take two hours to finish.
- Add a lot of cutscenes.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- Add an earlier “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” Venom fight intended to grant a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added face details to `makePerson` and retained MJ’s explicit woman/long-hair configuration.
- Added intro-screen markup, start flow, and intro styling.
- Added cinematic overlay markup/styles and story-scene data for campaign missions.
- Added a first-contact Venom mission before “NIGHT SHIFT.”

### Active
- Wire the cinematic scene data to gameplay, including advancing/skipping scenes and triggering scenes at mission starts and key story moments.
- Fix shard reward logic so the first Venom fight bonds the fragment immediately and persistently; current reward logic still checks only `m.finalBoss`.
- Expand campaign content and pacing toward the requested two-hour completion time.
- Verify gameplay, fix discovered bugs, and rerun syntax checks.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior attempt to start a server on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.

## Next Move
1. Update `updateMission()` so `m.firstBond` grants the shard on the first Venom defeat, sets bonded suit state, and keeps it available throughout the campaign.
2. Implement cinematic queue controls and lifecycle; connect scene data to `prepareMission()`, intro, first Venom encounter, and finale without letting gameplay proceed during scenes.
3. Add villain hair where appropriate, excluding Venom, and review face/model placement.
4. Expand and pace campaign content toward two hours.
5. Run `node --input-type=module --check < game.js`, verify gameplay in a browser on an available port, and fix issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Character models, missions, first-bond reward logic, cinematic scene data, controls, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Intro screen, cinematic overlay, HUD, menus, credits, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Intro and cinematic styling, UI, and responsive layout.

## Important Context
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Cinematic data is defined in `storyScenes`; state variables `cinematicActive`, `cinematicScenes`, and `cinematicIndex` exist, but no playback/advance/skip implementation is wired yet.
- `updateMission()` still grants the bond only when `m.finalBoss` is true; therefore the newly added `firstBond:true` mission does not yet grant it.
- Earlier work includes suit switching, four storefronts with health restoration, and a final Venom boss with an eight-hit health pool.
- Working files are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Add cinematic story scenes and bond the hero to a piece of Venom during their first fight; add hands to Spider-Man, MJ, all NPCs, and villains.

## Requirements
- Keep the hero, city, characters, and dialogue original; avoid copying existing games.
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- MJ is a woman; give her, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom.
- “Fix every bug You find”
- Campaign should take two hours to finish.
- Add a lot of cutscenes.
- Add hands for MJ, Spider-Man, all NPCs, and villains.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- Add an earlier “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” Venom fight intended to grant a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is explicitly configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added intro-screen markup and styling, plus cinematic overlay markup/styles and story-scene dialogue data.
- Added the first-contact Venom mission before “NIGHT SHIFT.”
- Updated `updateMission()` to grant the bonded shard for `m.firstBond` or `m.finalBoss`.

### Active
- Fulfill the new request by adding visible hands to the hero, MJ, NPCs, and villains.
- Wire cinematic playback, advancing/skipping, and lifecycle; trigger scenes at intro, mission starts, key story moments, and finale while preventing gameplay during scenes.
- Add villain hair where appropriate, excluding Venom, and review face/model placement.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward two hours.
- Run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification; fix discovered issues.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior attempt to start a server on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.

## Next Move
1. Add hand meshes to `makeHero()`, `makePerson()`, and `makeVillain()` so they fit each character’s arms and suit/materials.
2. Implement cinematic queue controls and connect scenes to game start and mission/story transitions.
3. Review villain character details and add appropriate hair, excluding Venom.
4. Expand and pace the campaign toward the requested two-hour duration.
5. Run `node --input-type=module --check < game.js`, verify gameplay in a browser using an available port, and fix issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Character models, missions, shard reward logic, cinematic scene data, controls, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Intro screen, cinematic overlay, HUD, menus, credits, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Intro and cinematic styling, UI, and responsive layout.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Cinematic data is defined in `storyScenes`; `cinematicActive`, `cinematicScenes`, and `cinematicIndex` exist, but playback and advancement are not wired.
- `updateMission()` now bonds the shard on first Venom defeat via `m.firstBond`; suit switching is available thereafter.
- Earlier work includes suit switching, four storefronts with health restoration, and a final Venom boss with an eight-hit health pool.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Add cinematic story scenes, a persistent Venom shard bond, visible hands, and action-game combat against thugs and villains.

## Requirements
- Keep the hero, city, characters, and dialogue original; avoid copying existing games.
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- MJ is a woman; give her, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom.
- Add hands for Spider-Man, MJ, all NPCs, and villains.
- Add combat for fighting thugs and villains.
- “Fix every bug You find”
- Campaign should take two hours to finish, with lots of cutscenes.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- Add an earlier “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” Venom fight intended to grant a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.
- Thug fights are being added as a dedicated mission, with punch controls and basic health-based enemies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is explicitly configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added intro-screen markup and styling, cinematic overlay markup/styles, and story-scene dialogue data.
- Added the first-contact Venom mission before “NIGHT SHIFT”; `updateMission()` grants the bonded shard for `m.firstBond` or `m.finalBoss`.
- Added hand/palm/finger meshes to the hero, civilian/MJ person model, and villain model.
- Updated HUD controls to indicate `CLICK / F` attack and added a mobile `PUNCH` action button.
- Added `attackArms` tracking to the hero model for attack animation.
- Added `makeThug()` for original procedural enemies with health and visual variation.
- Added an “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” thug mission to the campaign and created the `thugs` collection.

### Active
- Complete thug combat: spawn enemies for the new mission, implement player attacks/animation, enemy damage/defeat, and enemy attacks/player damage.
- Wire cinematic playback, advancing/skipping, and lifecycle; trigger scenes at intro, mission starts, key story moments, and finale while preventing gameplay during scenes.
- Review villain character details, face/model placement, and hair where appropriate, excluding Venom.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward the requested two-hour duration.
- Run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification; fix discovered issues.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior attempt to start a server on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.

## Next Move
1. Finish thug encounter spawning, attacks, damage feedback, enemy defeat, and combat controls for desktop and mobile.
2. Connect `storyScenes` to intro and mission/story transitions, including advancing/skipping and pausing gameplay during scenes.
3. Review and expand villain/campaign content, then check character details and hand placement.
4. Run `node --input-type=module --check < game.js`, verify gameplay in a browser using an available port, and fix discovered issues.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Character models, missions, thug scaffolding, shard reward logic, cinematic data, controls, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Intro screen, cinematic overlay, HUD, menus, credits, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Intro and cinematic styling, UI, and responsive layout.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are currently untracked in git status.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Cinematic data is defined in `storyScenes`; `cinematicActive`, `cinematicScenes`, and `cinematicIndex` exist, but playback and advancement are not wired.
- Current villain combat uses click-triggered attacks near bosses; the new thug-combat components are only scaffolding so far.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Update the graphics to evoke the 2004 Spider-Man game while keeping the hero, city, characters, and dialogue original.

## Requirements
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- MJ is a woman; give her, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom.
- Add hands for Spider-Man, MJ, all NPCs, and villains.
- Add combat for fighting thugs and villains.
- “Fix every bug You find”
- Campaign should take two hours to finish, with lots of cutscenes.
- On mission defeat, provide “Retry” or “cancel it.”
- Match the visual style of the 2004 Spider-Man game.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” Venom fight is intended to grant a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.
- Thug fights are a dedicated “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” mission with punch controls and health-based enemies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is explicitly configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added intro-screen markup and styling, cinematic overlay markup/styles, and story-scene dialogue data.
- Added the first-contact Venom mission and shard reward logic for `m.firstBond` or `m.finalBoss`.
- Added hand/palm/finger meshes to the hero, civilian/MJ person model, and villain model.
- Updated HUD to indicate attack controls and added a mobile `PUNCH` action button.
- Added hero attack-arm tracking and `makeThug()` with procedural clothing, health, and a health bar.
- Added the “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” mission and thug spawning/cleanup scaffolding; changed its mission locations to one encounter location.
- Began adding cinematic and combat state variables.

### Active
- Complete thug combat: player attack input and animation, thug damage/defeat, enemy attacks/player damage, and mission progress updates.
- Implement cinematic playback, advancing/skipping, and lifecycle at intro, mission starts, story moments, and finale while preventing gameplay during scenes.
- Add and wire a mission defeat choice with Retry and cancel actions.
- Review villain character details, face/model placement, and hair where appropriate, excluding Venom.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward the requested two-hour duration.
- Update graphics to evoke the 2004 Spider-Man game without copying protected characters or assets.
- Run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification; fix discovered issues.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior attempt to start a server on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.
- A bulk edit of `prepareMission()` failed because exact source text did not match; the current code still creates thug mission targets as `signal`, spawns thugs for every thug mission place, and plays mission voice immediately.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `game.js` edits and finish `prepareMission()` so thug targets are typed correctly and spawn a single set of five enemies.
2. Implement attack input, player/enemy damage, defeat handling, and mission progress for thugs.
3. Add defeat UI choices “Retry” and “Cancel mission,” and define cancel behavior.
4. Wire cinematics to intro and mission/story transitions, including advancing/skipping and pausing gameplay.
5. Apply an original visual treatment inspired by the 2004 Spider-Man game, then run syntax checks and verify gameplay in a browser on an available port.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, procedural characters, missions, cinematic data, thug scaffolding, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Intro screen, cinematic overlay, HUD, menus, defeat UI, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Visual styling for menus, cinematic overlay, HUD, and responsive controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are currently untracked in git status.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Cinematic data is defined in `storyScenes`, but playback is not wired.
- Current villain combat uses click-triggered attacks near bosses; thug combat remains incomplete.
- Current defeat UI has retry and main-menu options; mission-specific cancel behavior is not implemented.

## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Update the graphics to evoke the 2004 Spider-Man game while keeping the hero, city, characters, and dialogue original.

## Requirements
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- MJ is a woman; give her, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom.
- Add hands for Spider-Man, MJ, all NPCs, and villains.
- Add combat for fighting thugs and villains.
- “Fix every bug You find”
- Campaign should take two hours to finish, with lots of cutscenes.
- On mission defeat, provide “Retry” or “cancel it.”
- Match the visual style of the 2004 Spider-Man game without copying protected characters or assets.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” Venom fight is intended to grant a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.
- Thug fights are a dedicated “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” mission with punch controls and health-based enemies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is explicitly configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added hand/palm/finger meshes to hero, civilian/MJ, and villain models.
- Added intro and cinematic overlay markup/styles, cinematic dialogue data, and initial cinematic playback functions.
- `prepareMission()` now classifies thug targets as `thug`, removes associated character objects during cleanup, and resets mission defeat state.
- Added “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” mission, five-enemy spawn scaffolding, thug procedural model with health bar, HUD punch hint, and mobile `PUNCH` button.

### Active
- Finish mission cinematic wiring: `prepareMission()` currently ends after the toast and does not start `storyScenes`; wire cinematic controls (`cinematicNext`, `cinematicSkip`) and pause gameplay during playback.
- Implement player attack input/animation, thug damage/defeat, enemy attacks/player damage, and mission progress for thugs.
- Add defeat UI choices “Retry” and “Cancel mission,” and define cancel behavior.
- Review villains’ face/model details and hair where appropriate, excluding Venom.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward the requested two-hour duration.
- Update graphics to evoke the 2004 Spider-Man game using original assets and design.
- Run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification; fix discovered issues.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior attempt to start a server on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.

## Next Move
1. Wire `prepareMission()` into story-scene playback and ensure cinematic advance/skip actions work; keep gameplay disabled until playback ends.
2. Implement attack and thug combat, including enemy damage and defeat handling.
3. Add retry/cancel-mission choices to defeat UI and implement their outcomes.
4. Refine visuals and campaign pacing, then run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification on a confirmed available port.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, procedural characters, missions, cinematics, thug scaffolding, combat, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Intro, cinematic overlay, HUD, defeat UI, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Visual styling for menus, cinematics, HUD, and responsive controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Cinematic helpers exist, but `prepareMission()` currently does not launch them, and cinematic buttons are not wired.
- Current villain combat uses click-triggered attacks near bosses; thug combat remains incomplete.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Update the visuals to evoke the 2004 Spider-Man game while keeping characters, city, and dialogue original; user additionally asked, “Also make Venoms Model Like this.”

## Requirements
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- MJ is a woman; give her, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom.
- Add hands for Spider-Man, MJ, all NPCs, and villains.
- Add combat for fighting thugs and villains.
- Fix every bug found.
- Campaign should take two hours to finish, with lots of cutscenes.
- On mission defeat, provide “Retry” or “cancel it.”
- Match the visual style of the 2004 Spider-Man game without copying protected characters or assets.
- Make Venom’s model match the user’s referenced example; the example/reference is not present in the available conversation context.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” is intended to grant a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.
- Thug fights are a dedicated “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” mission with punch controls and health-based enemies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is explicitly configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added hand/palm/finger meshes to hero, civilian/MJ, and villain models.
- Added intro and cinematic overlay markup/styles, cinematic dialogue data, and initial cinematic playback functions.
- `prepareMission()` classifies thug targets as `thug`, removes associated character objects during cleanup, and resets mission defeat state.
- Added “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” mission, five-enemy spawn scaffolding, thug procedural model with health bar, HUD punch hint, and mobile `PUNCH` button.
- Added cinematic line display, next/skip callbacks, and `playCinematic()`/`finishCinematic()` helpers in `game.js`.
- Added story scene dialogue for “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” to `storyScenes`.

### Active
- Wire `prepareMission()` into story-scene playback so gameplay stays paused until scenes finish; current `prepareMission()` still ends after the toast and does not start cinematics.
- Implement player attack input/animation, thug damage/defeat, enemy attacks/player damage, and thug mission progress.
- Add defeat UI choices “Retry” and “Cancel mission,” and implement their outcomes. Current UI has retry and main-menu buttons, not cancel mission.
- Refine villains’ faces/model details and hair where appropriate, excluding Venom.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward the requested two-hour duration.
- Update visuals to the requested 2004-game-inspired style using original assets/design.
- Address the Venom model reference request once the reference/example is available.
- Run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification; fix discovered issues.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior server attempt on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.
- Venom’s requested “like this” model reference is unavailable in the visible conversation context.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and wire cinematic playback in `prepareMission()`; ensure missions remain inactive while a scene is playing.
2. Implement attack input and complete thug combat, including enemy attacks and defeat progress.
3. Add retry/cancel-mission defeat options and working outcomes.
4. Ask for or locate the Venom visual reference, then adjust the procedural model accordingly.
5. Refine campaign pacing and visuals, then run syntax checks and browser verification on a confirmed available port.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, procedural characters, missions, cinematics, thug scaffolding, combat, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Intro, cinematic overlay, HUD, defeat UI, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Visual styling for menus, cinematics, HUD, and responsive controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Cinematic helpers use `cinematicScenes`, `cinematicIndex`, `cinematicActive`, `cinematicNext`, `cinematicSkip`, and `cinematicDone`; button event wiring still needs verification.
- Existing `prepareMission()` ends with a toast and does not activate `storyScenes`; the attempted targeted edits to add the playback call failed.
- Existing click handling starts a web swing and can damage a nearby boss, but thug combat is not implemented.
- Existing defeat UI’s `retry-btn` restarts the entire patrol; `return-menu-btn` returns to the main menu.

## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Update the visuals to evoke the 2004 Spider-Man game while keeping characters, city, and dialogue original; adjust Venom’s model to match the attached reference.

## Requirements
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- Give MJ, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom; add hands for the hero, MJ, NPCs, and villains.
- Add combat against thugs and villains, and offer “Retry” or “Cancel mission” after defeat.
- Aim for a campaign that takes two hours to finish, with many cutscenes.
- Keep characters, city, and dialogue original; don’t copy protected characters or assets.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” grants a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.
- “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” is a dedicated five-thug combat mission.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is explicitly configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added hand meshes to hero, civilians/MJ, and villains.
- Added mission story scenes and connected cinematic playback to mission preparation; added cinematic next/skip button handlers and Enter/Escape controls.
- Added thug models, health bars, five-thug spawn scaffolding, punch input for keyboard/mobile, thug health/damage, thug pursuit/attacks, and thug mission progress.
- Added “Cancel Mission” to the defeat UI and wired retry to restart the current mission.
- Prevented mission activity while cinematics are playing and made mission completion pause gameplay.

### Active
- Refine the Venom model to match the user’s attached reference image.
- Refine villain faces/models and update the game’s visual style while keeping all designs original.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward the requested two-hour duration.
- Run syntax checks and browser gameplay verification; fix bugs found.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been performed; a prior server attempt on port `3002` failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and that port was not confirmed to serve the project.
- The Venom reference image was attached in the conversation, but its details are not preserved in the available text context; inspect the attachment if accessible before modeling.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current changes in `game.js` and run syntax checks; verify cinematic progression, combat, and defeat/retry/cancel behavior.
2. Start the project on a confirmed available port and test gameplay in a browser.
3. Review the attached Venom reference and adjust the procedural model accordingly.
4. Continue polishing original visuals and campaign pacing toward the requested duration.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, procedural characters, missions, cinematics, thug combat, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Intro, cinematic overlay, HUD, defeat options, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Visual styling for menus, cinematics, HUD, and responsive controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- The user’s newest request was “Also make Venoms Model Like this,” with an attached JPEG reference; this model adjustment remains unresolved.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Improve collision and add grounded, weighty explosions without making the game goofy.

## Requirements
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- Give MJ, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom; add hands for the hero, MJ, NPCs, and villains.
- Add thug and villain combat; after defeat, offer “Retry” or “Cancel mission.”
- Aim for a two-hour campaign with many cutscenes.
- Keep characters, city, and dialogue original; don’t copy protected characters or assets.
- Keep buildings off streets, prevent walking through buildings and objects, and add “Hevy” explosions that feel serious rather than goofy.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” grants a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.
- “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” is a dedicated five-thug combat mission.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added hand meshes to the hero, civilians/MJ, and villains.
- Added story cinematics with next/skip controls and keyboard progression.
- Added five-thug spawning, health bars, punch controls, thug pursuit/attacks, and mission progress.
- Added defeat UI with retry/cancel options; retry restarts the current mission.
- Prevented mission activity during cinematics and paused gameplay after mission completion.
- Fixed cinematic keyboard handling so Escape skips scenes before pause handling; `resumeGame()` and `restart()` no longer activate gameplay during a cinematic.
- Ran `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` successfully before the latest edits.

### Active
- Arrange building footprints so buildings do not occupy streets; add collision for buildings and relevant objects.
- Add weighty, grounded explosions consistent with the game’s tone.
- Refine the Venom model using the user’s reference image, if accessible.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward the requested duration.
- Verify gameplay, controls, cinematics, combat, and defeat/retry/cancel behavior in a browser.

### Blocked
- Browser verification is pending: a local server was started on port `4173`, and a Chromium screenshot command is running in the background without a reported result.
- The Venom reference image was attached earlier but is not present in the preserved text context or repository files.

## Next Move
1. Implement building placement and collision that respect street boundaries; cover other solid world objects as appropriate.
2. Add serious, restrained explosion effects and verify their performance and tone.
3. Inspect the Venom reference if available and adjust the procedural model.
4. Finish browser verification, then continue campaign pacing and visual polish.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World generation, collision, characters, missions, cinematics, combat, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Menus, HUD, cinematic overlay, defeat options, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Menus, cinematics, HUD, and responsive controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in git status.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Browser screenshot command targets `http://127.0.0.1:4173/` and `/tmp/opencode/afterlight.png`; it has not yet been confirmed complete.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an original browser-playable 3D superhero city adventure with a long campaign, traversal, missions, characters, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Improve collisions, combat timing, and character movement animations.

## Requirements
- Include swinging, wall climbing, cars, NPC conversations, water/drowning, missions, menus, credits, voice lines, shops, street details, and clear controls.
- Give MJ, pedestrians, and villains faces and varied hair, except Venom; add hands for the hero, MJ, NPCs, and villains.
- Add thug and villain combat; after defeat, offer “Retry” or “Cancel mission.”
- Aim for a two-hour campaign with many cutscenes.
- Keep characters, city, and dialogue original; don’t copy protected characters or assets.
- Keep buildings off streets, prevent walking through buildings and objects, and make “Hevy” explosions feel serious rather than goofy.
- Add animations for walking, swinging, climbing, and villains; improve attack timing.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural models and world geometry, HTML overlays, and browser speech synthesis.
- Structure the campaign as mission threads, ending in a dedicated Venom boss fight.
- “FIRST CONTACT: THE LIVING SHARD” grants a persistent shard bond and black-suit switching.
- “UNDERPASS AMBUSH” is a dedicated five-thug combat mission.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added facial details and varied hair to procedural people; MJ is configured as a woman with long hair.
- Added hand meshes to the hero, civilians/MJ, and villains.
- Added story cinematics with next/skip controls and keyboard progression.
- Added five-thug spawning, health bars, thug pursuit/attacks, and mission progress.
- Added defeat UI with retry/cancel options; retry restarts the current mission.
- Prevented mission activity during cinematics and paused gameplay after mission completion.
- Fixed cinematic keyboard handling so Escape skips scenes before pause handling; `resumeGame()` and `restart()` no longer activate gameplay during a cinematic.
- Reworked building placement into block interiors with street setbacks; added collision checks for buildings, roadside fixtures, shops, and cars in `blocked()`.
- Added restrained impact effects in `game.js`: short-lived core, expanding dust and ring, and bouncing fragments; thug and boss defeats trigger effects.
- Tightened boss attack targeting in `attack()` to within 4.4 units; `resolveHeroAttack()` checks boss model position and a 4.8-unit range.
- Changed hero attacks to store a target and resolve once after a timed wind-up; thug and boss perfect counters deal extra damage and apply stagger.
- Added thug and boss attack wind-up, strike, cooldown, stagger, and movement/attack animation updates in the combat portion of `update(dt)`.

### Active
- Finish wiring animation rigs into player movement, swinging, climbing, and attack states; `heroArmPose` is currently calculated but unused, and `animateCharacter()` is not yet called for the hero.
- Review click-to-swing/attack input: the canvas click handler still directly damages nearby bosses with a 13-unit range, bypassing timed attacks; `interact()` also damages bosses directly.
- Check combat flow for duplicate boss damage: the objective-distance `bossAttack` logic still applies damage separately from timed boss strikes.
- Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify gameplay in a browser.
- Expand and pace campaign content toward the requested duration; refine Venom using the reference image if it becomes available.

### Blocked
- The Venom reference image from earlier is not available in the preserved conversation context or repository files.

## Next Move
1. Wire `heroArmPose` and `animateCharacter()` to the hero’s movement, swing, climb, and timed attack phases.
2. Remove or reconcile direct boss damage from canvas click and `interact()` with the timed attack resolver; check for overlapping boss damage paths.
3. Run syntax and diff checks, then verify combat and animations in a browser.
4. Continue campaign expansion and pacing.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World generation, collisions, characters, missions, cinematics, combat, impacts, and in-progress animation/attack timing.
- `index.html`: Menus, HUD, cinematic overlay, defeat options, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Menus, cinematics, HUD, and responsive controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/afterlight.png`: Earlier browser screenshot, captured before the latest collision and animation edits.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear untracked in git status.
- Boss mission target positions and villain model positions differ; attack range checks should use the villain position where applicable.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Latest combat and animation edits have not been syntax-checked or browser-tested.
